metaDescription: Digital marketing for Texas businesses: SEO, Google and Meta ads, social media, websites and video for Houston, Dallas-Fort Worth, Austin, San Antonio and beyond.
lead: TDM (The Digital Marketing Services) is a digital marketing agency that works with Texas businesses on SEO, paid advertising, social media, websites and video. Texas is large enough that its big metros act like separate states, each with its own industries, costs and competitors. We work with Texas companies remotely and plan campaigns metro by metro, in English and with Spanish where your customers use it.

sections.heading: Four metros that do not behave alike
paragraphs: Houston is built on energy, the port, and one of the largest medical complexes in the world. It is also among the most diverse cities in the country, so audiences and languages vary widely from one part of town to the next. Dallas-Fort Worth is a corporate and logistics centre, home to many company headquarters, with affluent suburbs such as Plano and Frisco where much of the consumer spending sits.

Austin is the state capital and its technology hub, with a large university and a young, online-first population that responds to brand and content more than to hard selling. San Antonio combines military bases, tourism around the River Walk and the Alamo, and a majority-Hispanic population with deep local roots.

Outside the big four, the picture changes again. El Paso and the Rio Grande Valley are border economies where business is routinely done in two languages. Midland and Odessa rise and fall with oil activity in the Permian Basin.

sections.heading: Distance changes how people search
paragraphs: Texans drive, and they judge a business partly by how far away it is. In the sprawling metro areas, people search by suburb or by the highway they live near: Katy, The Woodlands, Sugar Land, Arlington, Round Rock. A service firm with one office and a wide territory needs area pages and a properly set service area in its business profile, or it will only appear for searches made close to its front door.

The weather sets part of the calendar. Long, hot summers make air conditioning repair an emergency purchase, and hail and severe storms drive sudden demand for roofing and car body repair. Campaigns for home services should be ready to scale within hours when conditions change.
bullets: Separate campaigns and budgets for each metro, never one statewide ad group.
Suburb-level landing pages for businesses that serve wide areas.
Call tracking, since many Texas service customers still pick up the phone.
Seasonal budgets for trades tied to heat and storms.

sections.heading: Spanish, English and both
paragraphs: A large share of Texans are Hispanic, and Spanish is common at home and at work, most of all in San Antonio, El Paso, the Valley and much of Houston. Many customers are fully bilingual and move between languages without thinking about it. Good bilingual marketing here is written for Texans of Mexican heritage, not copied from a campaign made for Miami or Madrid: vocabulary, references and tone differ.
We decide where Spanish belongs by looking at your existing customers and at the search terms used in your area, then build the pages, ads and replies to match.

sections.heading: Business-to-business in the Texas economy
paragraphs: Much of the state's economy sells to other companies: oilfield services, engineering, construction, logistics, software. These buyers take longer to decide and involve more people. For them we concentrate on search visibility for specific technical needs, clear capability and case pages on the site, and paid campaigns aimed at job roles rather than broad audiences. Local identity also carries weight in Texas, so a firm that is Texas owned and operated should say so plainly.

cards.heading: Texas sectors we plan campaigns for

items.title: Energy and oilfield services
items.text: Houston and Permian Basin suppliers need technical content and targeted outreach to engineers and procurement teams.

items.title: Home services
items.text: HVAC, roofing, plumbing and pest control firms compete in the map results across fast-growing suburbs.

items.title: Healthcare
items.text: Practices and clinics around the big medical centres need clear service pages, reviews and compliant ad wording.

items.title: Technology and SaaS
items.text: Austin and Dallas software firms need search content, paid acquisition and sites that turn trials into customers.

items.title: Restaurants and food brands
items.text: Tex-Mex, barbecue and new concepts rely on short video, local search and an active social presence.

items.title: Construction and real estate
items.text: Builders, developers and agents market to newcomers arriving from other states.

presence: We work with Texas businesses remotely. Meetings are held by video call, reporting is shared online, and strategy, design, development and video are delivered by one team.

faqs.q: Do you have an office in Texas?
faqs.a: No. We work with businesses in Texas remotely, by video call and shared reporting, with a plan and schedule agreed with you.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to hire a marketing agency in Texas?
faqs.a: It depends on scope: the channels, the number of locations and how competitive your trade is in your metro. We quote after a free consultation.

faqs.q: Should I advertise differently in Houston and Dallas?
faqs.a: Yes. The industries, suburbs, competitors and ad costs are different. We set up each metro as its own campaign with its own keywords, pages and budget.

faqs.q: Do Texas businesses need Spanish-language ads?
faqs.a: Many do, particularly in San Antonio, El Paso, the Rio Grande Valley and parts of Houston. We check who your customers are before recommending Spanish or bilingual campaigns.

faqs.q: How soon will I see results from SEO in Texas?
faqs.a: It depends on your requirements, your starting point and the competition in your market. The timeline is agreed in the plan before work begins.
